Very few supplements have an evidence base this consistent. Given that, the only real question is whether the powder in the tub is what the label says, which is why third-party verification dominates my scoring here.

highlights.title: Buy powder rather than gummies if you want a verified dose
highlights.body: Testing published this year identified real limitations in third-party analysis of creatine gummies, and independent checks have repeatedly found gummies delivering less creatine than labelled because the compound degrades to creatinine in that format. Gummies are a convenience format with a documented stability problem. Powder mixes into anything and costs less per gram.

highlights.title: Optimum Nutrition is the sensible default for most people
highlights.body: It delivers micronized monohydrate at commodity pricing with adequate testing, and monohydrate is the form every major trial used. More expensive forms marketed as better absorbed have far thinner evidence behind them. Buy plain monohydrate from a brand that publishes testing, take 3 to 5 grams daily, and ignore the formulation upsell.

en.commentary: Thorne Creatine keeps first place, and independent testing this cycle makes the case for tested brands unusually concrete. ConsumerLab tested eleven popular creatine products and found one failing quality standards, and separate testing found four of six creatine gummies sold on Amazon contained essentially no creatine at all. That gummy result is the number worth remembering. It means an entire popular format is currently unreliable, and anyone taking creatine in gummy form should verify their specific product or move back to powder. Thorne holds the top spot on pharmaceutical grade quality control and consistent third party verification, which is exactly the assurance those test results show is missing elsewhere. Optimum Nutrition sits second and remains the sensible mainstream buy, delivering micronized monohydrate at a fair price from a supply chain with a long clean record. Momentous takes third on NSF certification, which matters for tested athletes. Transparent Labs holds fourth and Legion fifth. The same testing round also noted that some products are priced nearly three times higher than necessary for equivalent quality, which is the other lesson here. Creatine monohydrate is a commodity when it is properly made, and paying a premium buys verification rather than a better molecule. Buy a tested monohydrate powder, take five grams daily, and ignore every proprietary variant marketed as an upgrade.

references.title: Momentous launches Signature Spec Creatine with tenfold tighter purity controls and PFAS screening
Best Third-Party Tested Creatine Supplements in 2026
Is Your Product Ready to Be Listed? What the Dietary Supplement Listing Act of 2026 Means for Your Business

en.commentary:
Momentous moves up to second, and this is the clearest testing-driven ranking change I have made all year. The company launched Signature Spec Creatine with six-stage independent testing, tenfold tighter purity controls and PFAS screening on top of NSF Certified for Sport status. PFAS screening is the part that matters. Nobody else in this category is testing for it, and given how widely those compounds turn up in processed ingredients, being first to screen is a genuine differentiator rather than a marketing line.

Thorne holds first place because it has been doing this consistently for years. Its creatine is NSF Certified for Sport with published certificates of analysis, and the manufacturing quality has never given me a reason to look elsewhere. Consistency across batches over a long period is what earns the top spot in a supplement category, because the failure mode here is a bad lot rather than a bad formula.

Creatine monohydrate is chemically simple and every product on this list delivers the same molecule. That is precisely why testing dominates my scoring. Independent analysis has repeatedly found products underdosed against label, contaminated with heavy metals, or padded with undisclosed fillers. The molecule is not the risk. The supply chain is.

The Dietary Supplement Listing Act of 2026, introduced in April as H.R. 8370, would create the first mandatory FDA product-listing regime for supplements. It stops short of pre-market approval, and it would still make the market considerably more transparent than it is today. Brands already publishing full certificates of analysis have nothing to fear from it, which tells you something about who to buy from now.

highlights.title: Momentous takes second because PFAS screening is genuinely new
highlights.body: Signature Spec Creatine ships with six-stage independent testing, tenfold tighter purity controls and PFAS screening alongside NSF Certified for Sport status. The PFAS testing is the meaningful part, because nobody else in this category screens for those compounds and they turn up widely across processed ingredient supply chains. Being first to look for a contaminant others ignore is a real differentiator, and it earns a two-tenth increase and second place.

highlights.title: Every product here contains the same molecule, so buy the testing
highlights.body: Creatine monohydrate is chemically simple and identical across every product on this board. Independent analysis has repeatedly turned up products underdosed against their own label, contaminated with heavy metals, or padded with undisclosed fillers. The molecule carries no risk at all. The supply chain carries all of it. That is why third-party certification dominates my scoring here more heavily than in any other supplement category.

highlights.title: Thorne holds first on batch-to-batch consistency over years
highlights.body: NSF Certified for Sport status with published certificates of analysis, and a manufacturing record that has stayed clean across a long period. In supplements the realistic failure mode is a single bad lot rather than a flawed formula, so what earns the top position is consistency measured in years. Thorne has that record, and until a competitor matches the duration rather than the specification, first place stays here.

highlights.title: The Listing Act would make this market considerably more transparent
highlights.body: H.R. 8370, introduced in April, would create the first mandatory FDA product-listing regime for dietary supplements, requiring a product-by-product submission rather than a one-time company registration. It stops short of pre-market approval and adds no new evidentiary burden on claims. Brands already publishing full certificates of analysis face no disruption from it, which is a useful signal about which companies to buy from right now.

zh-tw.commentary:
Momentous 升到第二，這是我今年做過最明確、由檢驗驅動的排名變動。它推出的 Signature Spec Creatine 有六階段獨立檢驗、純度管控收緊十倍，還加上 PFAS 篩檢，本來就有 NSF Certified for Sport 認證。重點是 PFAS 篩檢這件事。這個類別目前沒有別家在驗，而那類化合物在加工原料供應鏈裡出現的範圍很廣，第一個開始驗的人是真的做出差異，不是喊口號。

Thorne 守住第一，因為它這件事已經穩定做了很多年。它的肌酸有 NSF Certified for Sport 認證，檢驗報告公開，製造品質從來沒讓我想找別家。在補充品這個類別，長時間的批次一致性才是第一名的門檻，因為這裡的失敗模式是「某一批出問題」，而不是「配方不好」。

肌酸單水合物化學結構很單純，這張榜上每一罐給你的都是同一個分子。正因為如此，我的評分才會被檢驗主導。獨立檢驗一再驗出劑量不足、重金屬超標、或摻了沒標示的填充物的產品。分子本身沒有風險，風險全部在供應鏈。

四月提出的 2026 年膳食補充品登錄法案（H.R. 8370）會建立美國第一個強制性的 FDA 產品登錄制度。它沒有走到上市前審查，但已經會讓市場比現在透明很多。本來就把完整檢驗報告公開的品牌完全不會受影響，這件事本身就告訴你現在該買誰。

highlights.body: NSF Certified for Sport 認證加上公開的檢驗報告，而且長時間下來的製造紀錄一直很乾淨。補充品實際會出事的是某一批貨，而不是配方本身，所以拿第一名要看的是用年為單位衡量的穩定度。Thorne 有這個紀錄，在對手追上的是「年資」而不只是「規格」之前，第一名不會換人。

highlights.body: 四月提出的 H.R. 8370 會建立美國第一個強制性的 FDA 膳食補充品產品登錄制度，而且是逐項產品送件，不是公司登記一次就好。它沒有走到上市前審查，也沒有對宣稱增加新的舉證責任。本來就公開完整檢驗報告的品牌完全不受影響，這其實是個很好用的訊號，告訴你現在該買哪些公司。
